depthcharge: Write vendor data to ro vpd This change does two things, first the SRWD bit must be 0 and the vendor data contents must be all spaces in order for the vendor data to be settable in the vboot ui. Next when VbExSetVendorData is called the current VPD is read from flash, modified with the new data and written back to flash. This change does not enable the SRWD bit because whenever the system boots with SRWD cleared all of the block protect bits are also cleared. I'm not sure why the block protect bits are being cleared and if they are not set correctly the RO firmware will not be protected. BUG=b:124297157 TEST=Verified on an Arcada device that if serial_number is set to all spaces and SRWD is not set then a new serial number can be entered and read successfully from userspace using "vpd -l". Also verified that the serial number cannot be set if it is already set or SRWD is set. BRANCH=none Change-Id: I1b8d19d19e7bc6d93dc369ab53ee658782838077 Signed-off-by: Mathew King <mathewk@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1483996 Reviewed-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org>

cryptohome: fix IsAttestaionPrepared for tpm2 After CL:1418984, TpmIsAttestationPrepared in cryptohomed uses GetEnrollmentPreparations to get "is prepared" status in the "distributed" (TPM 2.0) case. Before this CL, it was just returning TRUE if there was at least one element in the returned enrollment_preparations map. That was wrong, since GetEnrollmentPreparations returns a map with true/false values for all known ACA types. So, even when the attestation is not prepared yet, the map is not empty, just all values are false. This CL fixes the logic and checks if there is at least one true value in the map instead. BUG=b:124085203 TEST=Run "cryptohome --action=tpm_attestation_status" on an unowned device with TPM2.0; check that "Attestation Prepared: false". Repeat after going through owning and preparing for attestation, check that "Attestation Prepared: true" this time. chromeos-bootimage: use altfw payload hashing for all The primary purpose of this change is to add the hash for the diag payload. The only remaining payload that isn't hashed is seabios, so I added that for the sake of consistency (under the assumption that just because a hash is there it doesn't mean it has to be used, and seabios is now opt-in on master so it shouldn't slow down the common case). This change also changes the name of the hash file from altfw_hash/${name}.sha256 to altfw/${name}.sha256 to make it easier for the firmware to derive the hash file name from the image name (by merely appending .sha256). clock: define the function clock_enable_module to all EC chips The API clock_enable_module(MODULE_FAST_CPU, x) allows common layer code to set the CPU frequency to turbo or normal when it is needed. However, not all of the EC chips support/implement the function. It causes build error if this function is added to the common codes which most of EC chips will use (EX: vboot_hash.) This CL fixes this issue by defining the function as weak by default. This CL also implements the clock_enable_module function for NPCX7 chip. BRANCH=none BUG=b:77608104 TEST=pass "make buildall" TEST=on npcx7_evb/yorp, with follow-up CL, check that security computation becomes faster and the clock goes back to normal frequency after the computation finishes.
